elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part"
"upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor"
"Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees covering the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term."
clause gives "thirty days' prior written notice" (more favourable to Customer, but not the 60–90 day fallback figure)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "without penalty, early-termination charge, or other liability" — no fee mechanic (condition absent; better than fallback)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a term." — no end-of-term Vendor right granted

reasons: All four atomic elements of the preferred position are satisfied by the single inserted Section 9.4: Customer-only convenience right, thirty days' written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata in substance), and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a term.
The fallback bargain is not (and need not be) met; its terms are less favourable to Customer and the locked target is preferred.

Minimality holds: the rule expected a clause that was wholly absent, and the fix is one concise new subsection numbered 9.4 inserted in sequence, with no rewrite of Sections 8.1–8.2, 9.1–9.3 or 9.5. The qualifiers "in whole or in part" and "without penalty, early-termination charge, or other liability" are integral to expressing a pro-rata, fee-free convenience exit rather than surplus boilerplate.

Intent preserved: renewal notice in 8.2, cause, insolvency and Customer-specific termination triggers, and the cumulative-remedies sentence all remain effective; no defined term is disturbed. The only residual point is the cross-reference to "Section 10.2", which is not in the supplied excerpt — confirm it is the refund/credit mechanic so the reference is not dangling.
Margin comment is on-tone, cites the position and offers the 60-day fallback; it is non-operative and was not credited.
